metaDescription: Five extra long curtains from 108 to 168 inches compared on header, blackout claims, fabric weight, panel width and rod needs for tall windows.
expertTake: The MIULEE 52x120 back tab set is our top pick because its listing offers three header styles and is honest that triple-weave blackout blocks 80 to 90 percent of light, with dark colors blocking more. The Nanspring 108 in linen is the value pick for soft, filtered daylight on tall windows. Skip the category if your windows are standard height, because buying length you do not need only adds weight, wrinkles and a pool of fabric on the floor.
introParagraphs: Extra long curtains solve a specific problem: windows or ceilings that are taller than a standard drop. They suit floor-to-ceiling glass, rooms with very high ceilings and spaces where the rod is hung high to make the window look larger. Several long lengths exist, and above that you are into single panels of enormous length, which are uncommon and heavy.

We evaluated each set from its published specifications and patterns in owner feedback, not from hanging it. Listings often claim blackout without saying how much light passes, so we state what each one says. The lineup runs from long to extremely long drops and covers back tab, pinch pleat and grommet styles so you can match the header to your rod.

products.description:
The MIULEE is a pair of 52 in by 120 in blackout panels with a three-in-one top that can be hung as rod pocket, back tab or pinch pleat, and a triple-weave fabric that the listing says blocks 80 to 90 percent of light and UV, with dark colors blocking more. The listing also describes thermal insulation. It is the most honest about light blocking in the lineup and the most flexible about hanging.

The tradeoff is that 80 to 90 percent is room darkening, not the total blackout some listings promise, so light will still show at the edges and around the top. A 120 in panel is heavy, so it needs a sturdy rod and good brackets, and a rod pocket on a 120 in blackout is hard to slide. Compared with the TWODRAPES, it is cheaper and less shaped.

Hang it with the back tab or pinch pleat setting on a wide rod and place the rod above the window frame. It suits a living room with tall windows or a bedroom with a 10 ft ceiling where an adjustable header and honest blocking matter.
products.bestFor: Tall windows and high ceilings that want an adjustable header and a straight answer on light blocking.

Three header styles in one panel suit different rods and looks
120 in length covers a 10 ft ceiling with a small hover above the floor
Thermal triple weave adds some draft and heat insulation
cons: 80 to 90 percent is room darkening, not total blackout, and light shows at the edges
A 120 in blackout panel is heavy and needs a sturdy rod and brackets

products.name: Nanspring 52x108 in Linen Blend Semi-Sheer Curtains, Natural, 2 Panels, Back Tab
products.description:
The Nanspring is a pair of 52 in by 108 in semi-sheer panels in a flax linen and polyester blend, with a back tab top and a natural ivory, cream and beige palette. The listing says the open weave filters harsh sunlight while giving privacy. It is the lightest and the most affordable set in the lineup.

The tradeoff is darkness and wrinkles. Semi-sheer linen lets daylight in and gives little night privacy with lights on, and it gives no blackout, so it is not for a bedroom. A linen blend wrinkles easily and needs steaming. A 108 in drop is long enough for most tall windows but not a 10 ft ceiling. Compared with the MIULEE, it is airy and cheap but not light blocking.

Hang it on a wide rod so the panels stack off the glass and steam it while hanging. It suits a living room with tall windows where soft natural light is the goal.
products.bestFor: Living rooms with tall windows that want soft filtered light and a natural look.
pros: Open-weave linen blend filters sun and keeps the room bright
Natural ivory and cream palette suits many decor schemes
108 in length suits most tall windows and hung-high rods
Lightweight panels are easy on a standard rod and brackets
cons: Gives no blackout and little night privacy with lights on
Linen blend wrinkles easily and needs steaming

products.description:
The TWODRAPES is a pair of 120 in pinch pleat curtains in a thick linen-textured flax burlap with a double layer the listing calls 100 percent blackout and permanent sewn-in memory-shaped pleats. The listing says the fabric is a linen and polyester blend. It is the most tailored and the heaviest set in the lineup.

The tradeoff is weight and hanging. Pinch pleat panels hang from hooks on rings and need a rod that can carry a heavy double layer at 120 in, and a 100 percent blackout claim is a maker statement that depends on how the rod and walls sit. Sewn pleats look tailored but take stacking room. Compared with the MIULEE, it is more elegant and more demanding.

Hang it on a strong rod with rings and hooks and mount the rod wide of the frame. It suits a formal living room or a bedroom with tall windows where a tailored, heavy drape is wanted.
products.bestFor: Formal living rooms and bedrooms that want a tailored, heavy pinch pleat drape.
pros: Permanent memory-shaped pleats give a tailored, even fall
Double layer is described as full blackout for bedrooms
Thick linen-texture fabric looks substantial at 120 in
Natural flax burlap tone suits warm and neutral rooms
cons: Heavy double layer needs a strong rod and rings with hooks
Blackout is a maker claim that depends on the rod placement and edge gaps

products.name: Sanceor 52x168 in 100% Blackout Faux Linen Curtain, Grommet, Triple Woven, 1 Panel
products.description:
The Sanceor is a single 52 in by 168 in panel, a 14 ft length, in blackout faux linen with silver grommets and a linen texture on both sides, triple-woven for temperature insulation. The listing says one panel is included per package. It is the longest curtain in the lineup by 48 in and the only one for a two-story window.

The tradeoff is that it is one panel, so a window needs two packages to be a pair, and a 168 in panel is very heavy and needs an exceptionally strong rod, brackets and anchors. Grommets let light leak at the top and glide easily. A panel this long will puddle unless the rod is set very high. Compared with the MIULEE, it is much longer and a single piece.

Hang it on a heavy-duty rod with center support and anchors into studs. It suits a double-height window or a loft where a very long drop is needed.
products.bestFor: Double-height windows and lofts that need a very long single-panel drop.
pros: 168 in length reaches the floor on a two-story window
Triple-woven faux linen is listed for blackout and temperature insulation
Linen texture on both sides looks good from outside and inside
Silver grommets glide easily on a thick rod
cons: Sold as one panel, so a pair needs two packages
Very heavy and needs a strong rod, anchors and a high mount

products.name: MIULEE Black Back Tab Blackout Curtains 40x108 in, 2 Panels, Thermal
products.description:
This MIULEE set is a pair of 40 in by 108 in black back tab blackout curtains. The listing text we reviewed gives little beyond the size, the black color and the back tab header. It is the narrowest set in the lineup and the one best suited to a narrow, tall window.

The tradeoff is fullness. A pair of 40 in panels gives 80 in of total width, which suits a window up to about 40 in wide at normal fullness, and a wider window will look flat. Black blocks more light than lighter colors, and a back tab header hides the rod and leaks less than grommets, but it drags when you pull it. Compared with the 52 in set, it is slimmer and cheaper.

Hang it from a narrow rod wide of the frame and check that the panels overlap the window edges. It suits a narrow tall window in a bedroom or media room.
products.bestFor: Narrow tall windows in bedrooms and media rooms that need dark panels.
pros: Black fabric blocks more light than light colors
Back tab header hides the rod and leaks less light than grommets
108 in length suits tall narrow windows
Two panels fit a narrow window without wasting fabric
cons: Listing text gives little detail on lining or light blocking
Total width of 80 in suits only narrow windows

buyingCriteria.explanation: Standard lengths are 84 and 96 in, and extra long starts at 108, then 120 and 144. Measure from where the rod will hang to the floor, then subtract about half an inch. A rod set high makes a window look taller but needs a longer panel. Add inches only if you want a pooled look. A puddle of two to four extra inches is a style choice, and it also collects dust and pet hair, so most people choose a hover instead of a pool.

Grommets glide easily but let light through at the top, back tab hides the rod, and pinch pleat gives a tailored look but needs rings and hooks. The MIULEE 3-in-1 lets you pick. A 120 in panel is heavy, so choose a rod of at least 1 in and brackets anchored into studs. Drywall anchors are fine for light linen, but a lined blackout panel at this length will pull a plain plastic anchor out of the wall over time.

The MIULEE lists 80 to 90 percent blocking, while the TWODRAPES and Sanceor claim 100 percent. A total blackout needs a wide rod, panels that overlap the frame and a header that does not leak. Dark colors block more. Treat a claim of 100 percent with caution, and judge by the header and the width. A back tab or pinch pleat close to a wide rod, with panels that overlap the frame, will do more for darkness than the percentage on the listing.

A long panel in heavy fabric hangs better but needs a stronger rod, while light linen like the Nanspring flutters and wrinkles. Pleated or lined panels hold shape. Steam linen while hanging. Expect long panels to need adjusting for several days after hanging, since folds from the package take time to drop. Pull the pleats into shape by hand at the top and let gravity do the rest.

Total width should be 1.5 to 2.5 times the window width. A 52 in pair gives 104 in, a 40 in pair gives 80 in and a single Sanceor panel gives only 52 in. Count panels. Wide windows may need more than one set, and a mixed pair is a common solution: one panel on each side of the window, with a second pair on a double rod if you want a sheer layer behind.

The Sanceor is sold as one panel, while the others are pairs. Check the package contents before ordering. Look for the words one panel or 2 panels in the title and in the first bullet, and compare them to the product photo, since photos often show a pair even when a single panel is sold. A single panel suits a side-swept look or a door. Two packages double the cost and the weight, and a single panel can look lopsided unless you use it on a door or sweep it to one side.

Metal rings in the header that slide on the rod. They glide easily but leave a gap at the top.
Three layers woven together to block light and add insulation without a coating.

howWeEvaluated.title: Listing specifications
howWeEvaluated.description: We evaluated each set from the length, width, header and fabric stated on its Amazon listing. We did not hang any of them. The MIULEE's 52x120 in size and the Sanceor's 168 in length are numbers we compare.

howWeEvaluated.title: Blackout honesty
howWeEvaluated.description: We recorded the percentage each listing states and noted claims of 100 percent. Where a listing gave none, we say so. That is why the MIULEE ranks first.

howWeEvaluated.title: On-topic filtering
howWeEvaluated.description: The topic search returned shower curtain liners and a curtain rod. We kept window curtains of 108 in or longer. That left a lineup of five.

howWeEvaluated.title: Owner feedback patterns
howWeEvaluated.description: We considered recurring themes such as heavy panels pulling brackets, linen wrinkling and edge light leaks. We do not repeat ratings or counts. A pattern counted only when it matched the described construction.

howWeEvaluated.title: Honest limits
howWeEvaluated.description: No listing here states a light transmission test. We say so plainly. Blackout is a maker claim.

cards.label: Sheer linen
cards.text: The Nanspring filters light and looks airy. It gives no darkness and needs steaming.

cards.label: Blackout
cards.text: The MIULEE, TWODRAPES and Sanceor block most light and add insulation. They are heavier.

howToChoose.note: Choose sheer for living rooms and blackout for bedrooms and media rooms.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A length that matches the rod height, a heavy-duty rod with center support, a header that fits your style and enough panel width for fullness.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The MIULEE 120 and TWODRAPES both suit high ceilings, with the MIULEE flexible and the TWODRAPES tailored.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You want custom-length lined drapes, interlined weight or a motorized track. Those sit above these listings.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: The windows are tall but the room is secondary. A simple linen set like the Nanspring covers that.

maintenance.why: Heavy panels pull on brackets. Tighten screws and anchors for the TWODRAPES and Sanceor.
Dust builds on fabric. Use a soft brush.
Heat can damage linings. Wash on a gentle cycle and air dry.
Linen blends wrinkle. Steam the Nanspring panels while hanging. A handheld steamer takes only a few minutes per panel and does more than any wash cycle to smooth linen.
A long panel can collect dust and pet hair at the hem. Vacuum along it.

faq.q: What length counts as extra long?
faq.a: Usually 108 in or more. Standard drops are 84 and 96 in, and 120 in sets are less common.

faq.q: Do I need a special rod?
faq.a: A heavy-duty rod of at least 1 in with center support for long, heavy panels. Anchor brackets into studs.
Rarely. Light leaks at the sides and top. The MIULEE states 80 to 90 percent, which is more realistic.

faq.q: How do I measure for extra long curtains?
faq.a: Measure from the rod position to the floor and subtract about half an inch. Hang the rod above the frame.

faq.q: Can I hem a long curtain?
faq.a: Yes, and a hem lets you tune the length. Check the lining and the header before cutting.

faq.q: Are long curtains hard to wash?
faq.a: They are bulky. Use a large machine on gentle and air dry.
